question: Will the Verkhovna Rada vote to extend martial law or general mobilization between October 15 and 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: An extension before Oct 31 is near-certain (20 straight cycles, ~310+ votes); the question is only the date. Recent extension votes were Tue/Wed: 21 Oct 2025 (15d before expiry), 14 Jan 2026 (Wed), 28 Apr 2026 (Tue, only 6d before expiry), 14 Jul 2026 (Tue, 19d). The Rada resumes plenary work Oct 12/13 (an extra Mon Oct 12 sitting was requested) with a crowded financing package due by Oct 15. If the extension is voted in that week, it would most likely be Oct 13-14 (outside the window), unless pushed to Thu Oct 15 or Fri Oct 16. A later plenary week (Oct 20-30) is also plausible given the April precedent. No human market found on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- Current regime: martial law + general mobilization extended July 14, 2026 (Tue) by laws 15401/15402 (313/311 votes), running Aug 2 -> Oct 31, 2026 (Ukrainska Pravda, 2026-07-14). July plenary week was Jul 14-15; the vote came on the first day (iz.com.ua).
- Earlier vote dates and lead times before expiry: Oct 21, 2025 (Tue), 15 days before the Nov 5 expiry, 317 votes (LB.ua 2025-10-21). Jan 14, 2026 (Wed), about 20 days before Feb 3. Apr 28, 2026 (Tue), only 6 days before May 4 (Ukrinform). Jul 14, 2026 (Tue), 19 days before Aug 2. In 2025: Jan 15 (Wed), Apr 16 (Wed), Jul 15 (Tue). Observed lead times range 6-23 days; every recent vote fell on a Tue or Wed.
- Plenary gap: no plenary sittings Sep 17 -> Oct 13, 2026, i.e. 26 days, attributed to security concerns (Hromadske 2026-09-29; Glavcom 2026-09-20). The plenary week was announced as starting Oct 12.
- Glavcom (2026-09-30): at the PM's request the Rada is convening early, with Mon Oct 12 proposed as an extra sitting day. A large package of laws and resolutions tied to about $29.5bn in international financing must pass by Oct 15. No mention of martial-law timing.
- Calendar: Oct 13 = Tue, Oct 14 = Wed (Defenders' Day), Oct 15 = Thu, Oct 16 = Fri, Oct 17 = Sat. The next plenary week after Oct 12-16 was not found (searched the meeting.rada.gov.ua calendar; dates not extractable).
- Not found: whether Zelensky has yet registered the decree-approval bills for the next cycle (searched, absent as of Oct 5); any MP (e.g. Zheleznyak) announcing a vote date.
- Status quo: an extension passes before Oct 31 (every cycle since 2022, 20 votes). The only uncertainty is which day.
- Resolution: resolves off a final adopting vote dated Oct 15, 16 or 17 (Kyiv) per rada.gov.ua or Ukrainska Pravda, not off committee approval or the presidential signature.
- Event window: Oct 15 00:00 -> Oct 17 24:00 Kyiv; as of Oct 5 the window has not started (0% elapsed).
- Markets: none found on Polymarket or Manifold (harness search plus own check).

Plenaries resume Oct 12/13 with an agenda reported for Oct 12-15, dominated by financing bills due by Oct 15. Recent extension votes fell on Tue/Wed, 6-20 days before expiry; Oct 13-15 fits the usual lead time, but a late-October sitting (as in April 2026) is also plausible. P(vote in the Oct 12-16 week) ~0.5-0.55 x P(Thu Oct 15 or Fri Oct 16 | that week) ~0.3, giving ~0.18. Thursday votes are uncommon but have happened (e.g. Jul 27, 2023). No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree the extension will pass and only the date is uncertain. Factual: the plenary block is reported as Oct 12-15 (extra Monday plus Tue-Thu), so Thu Oct 15 is the main qualifying day and Fri Oct 16 is a small tail. Run 3 is correct that Oct 14 is not a holiday (Defenders Day moved to Oct 1 in 2023; holidays are suspended under martial law anyway), so it is a normal sitting day. Whether late-October plenary weeks exist could not be settled from the dossiers, and that uncertainty is carried. Judgment: recent votes cluster on Tue/Wed, which favours Oct 13-14 over Oct 15, but the financing bills due by Oct 15 crowd the early days, and end-of-week votes have precedent. I would bet on ~0.18.
